dedupe_keys.name: aer floodscan daily flood fraction and admin level zonal statistics hdx

description: FloodScan uses satellite data to map and monitor floods daily so that current conditions can be compared with historical averages. The HDX dataset has two resources: a daily table of the average FloodScan Standard Flood Extent Depiction (SFED) flood fraction, from 0 to 100 percent, for first- and second-level administrative areas, with a historical day-of-year baseline and empirically estimated return periods; and a ZIP of daily gridded flood fraction for the last 90 days at about 10 km resolution (300 arcseconds), each file holding the SFED band and a baseline band. Baselines use the last ten years of data smoothed with an 11-day centred mean. The data come from AER's FloodScan, are modified and simplified by UN OCHA, and are published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange for a group of mainly African countries, updated weekly, as downloadable XLSX and GeoTIFF files under CC BY-IGO. Caveats: the open release carries only the last 90 days of gridded data, resolution is coarse, and flood fraction is not depth. It is useful for near-real-time hazard exposure monitoring, calibrating flood frequency in resilience studies and triggering emergency response; a related record is the FAO EVE flood monitoring system.
